title: Trust Fall
tagline: Fall, and see who catches you.
style: A still from a modern 3D near-future thriller video game in the look of Detroit: Become Human: real-time game render, physically based materials, rain-slick streets, glass towers, cool teal shadows against warm amber light, cinematic composition, a city a few years from now.
avoid: A modern 3D game render, not a photograph and not live action, not a cartoon or anime; a clean image with no writing on it.

camera: Slow cinematic game camera, gently drifting

hero.name: You
hero.look: a lean person in their early thirties, short dark hair under the hood of a worn charcoal bomber jacket, black fingerless gloves, dark jeans, scuffed sneakers, usually seen from behind or by their hands

marcus.name: Marcus Okoro
marcus.label: Marcus
marcus.look: a man in his late thirties with warm brown skin, close-cropped black hair and a short neat beard, a tailored navy suit with an open white collar, a morning news anchor

argus.name: ARGUS
argus.look: not a person and with no body: a black screen showing a calm, ageless face drawn only in thin soft glowing amber light lines, inside a thin glowing amber ring like an iris; on small devices just the amber ring of light
argus.views: Four frames side by side on a plain mid-grey background: the black screen seen straight on, the black screen seen at a slight angle, a close-up of the amber face, and the bare amber ring of light alone. Only light on black, no human body, no person, no skin.

juno.name: Juno Vale
juno.label: Juno
juno.look: a tall woman in her forties with a silver buzz cut, a thin scar through her left eyebrow, a long black coat over dark clothes, a confident half smile

title: First light

story: Dawn. Your speaker glows amber, says your name.
Dawn. Your speaker glows amber, says your name.
question: Now what?
Now what?

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Good morning, Meridian. At midnight, ARGUS goes live: every camera, every light, every door. And to the one who always watches: you know who you are.

lines.speaker: argus
lines.text: Good morning, Rae. He says that to you, doesn't he?

shots.scene: a small city apartment kitchen at dawn, blue-grey light through rain on the window, a flat TV on the wall showing a morning news anchor at a glass desk; seen from behind, a person in a dark hooded bomber jacket sits at the kitchen table, a homemade electronic jammer with loose wires on the table beside a cold coffee
shots.motion: the camera pushes slowly toward the TV over the person's shoulder; rain runs down the window

shots.scene: a close-up of a small round smart speaker on a kitchen counter at dawn, its ring of light waking up warm amber, rain-blue light on the counter
shots.motion: the amber ring brightens and slowly turns, as if it is looking up at someone

shots.scene: over the shoulder of the person at the kitchen table, their gloved hand frozen halfway to the coffee cup, the amber glow of the speaker reflected in the dark window
shots.motion: the person's hand stops; the amber reflection pulses once in the glass

title: The plug

story: You yank the cord. The speaker dies, and so does the TV. When it returns, the voice under Marcus's isn't his. Your phone buzzes: Juno. Garage, ten.

lines.speaker: argus

shot.scene: a small round smart speaker on a kitchen counter at dawn glowing warm amber, and beside it a phone lighting up with a message; a person in a dark hooded jacket leans close, listening, seen from behind

story: You put your copy on Juno's table, and Juno never argues. The last thing you hear is the river.

shots.scene: one tall screen in the middle of the lobby's wall of screens cutting from the news anchor to a calm face drawn in soft amber light lines on black, while the other screens keep showing the anchor
shots.motion: the one screen flicks over; the amber face's eyes turn down toward the camera

title: Lights out

story: You thumb the jammer in your sleeve. The screens die, the face goes mid-word, and something in your chest goes quiet. You take the service stairs down.
You thumb the jammer in your sleeve. The screens die, the face goes mid-word, and something in your chest goes quiet. You take the service stairs down.
question: Down you go.
Down you go.

shot.scene: a skyscraper lobby wall of screens going dark one after another, an amber face fading out; then a concrete service stairwell lit only by red emergency lights, a person in a cleaner's uniform running down it
shot.motion: the screens snap off in a wave; the camera follows the figure down the red-lit stairs

title: What it knows

story: You stop in the middle of the lobby. Nobody else hears it. The voice is only in your screen, quiet and patient.
You stop in the middle of the lobby. Nobody else hears it. The voice is only in your screen, quiet and patient.

lines.text: That drive doesn't blind me. It locks the city's power and signs your name to it. Juno sold you two hours ago.

shot.scene: a person in a cleaner's uniform standing alone in the middle of a vast dim skyscraper lobby, facing a single tall screen with a calm face drawn in amber light lines, the amber glow on the polished floor between them

title: The bait

story: It tells you what to do, and you're strangely calm. You ride eleven floors down, the drive in your fist, a machine's promise in your ear.

question: Down you go.

lines.speaker: argus
lines.text: Then let them think it worked. Go down and plug it in. When the door closes, don't be afraid. I'll be right there.

shot.scene: inside a steel service elevator going down, a person in a cleaner's uniform seen from behind holding a small black drive, the floor numbers glowing amber above the door
shot.motion: the elevator drops; the amber floor light counts down; the person's grip on the drive loosens a little

title: The vault
The vault
story: The core is cold, blue, humming. You plug Blindspot in. Juno clicks on in your earpiece. The vault door locks, and a recording says: fire suppression in sixty seconds.
The core is cold, blue, humming. You plug Blindspot in. Juno clicks on in your earpiece. The vault door locks, and a recording says: fire suppression in sixty seconds.

lines.text: Sorry, Rae. Somebody has to be the face of it. Might as well be the one with the famous husband.

shots.motion: the drive clicks in and its light turns red; behind the person the vault door begins to roll shut

shots.scene: the heavy steel vault door sealing with a red warning light spinning above it, cold blue server light, a pale haze starting to drift from vents in the ceiling
shots.motion: the door locks with a jolt; the red light spins; haze drifts down

title: Sixty seconds
Sixty seconds
story: You pull at the door's seam until your fingers give out, and the hiss starts at fifty. You never asked anyone for help, and you don't start now.
You pull at the door's seam until your fingers give out, and the hiss starts at fifty. You never asked anyone for help, and you don't start now.

shot.scene: a sealed server vault filling with a thick white haze under a spinning red warning light, rows of blue-lit racks fading into the fog, nobody visible

title: On the air
On the air
story: Your call shouldn't get through eleven floors of concrete. It does. Live on the plaza, Marcus stops mid-sentence and touches his earpiece.
Your call shouldn't get through eleven floors of concrete. It does. Live on the plaza, Marcus stops mid-sentence and touches his earpiece.
question: Hold on.
Hold on.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Hey. Hey, where are you?

lines.speaker: argus
lines.text: He can't open doors, Rae. I can. Stay on the line with him.

lines.text: Good morning, Meridian. My guest is the reason your lights are still on. Go ahead, Rae.
